title: Tension at highest point
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the tension in the rope at the highest point as 12 N, considering the total mass and centripetal force requirement.

title: Water pressure on cup
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the pressure (force) of the water on the cup bottom at the highest point as 9 N, derived from the normal force on the water.

title: Minimum speed for no spill
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the minimum speed at the highest point to prevent water from spilling, yielding approximately 3.16 m/s.

title: Force analysis for water
description: Important: Applies Newton's second law to the water alone to find the normal force from the cup, correctly using the water's mass and centripetal acceleration.

title: Force analysis for cup+water
description: Important: Applies Newton's second law to the combined cup-water system to find rope tension, correctly summing gravitational and centripetal forces.

title: Critical condition identification
description: Important: Identifies that the critical condition for water not spilling is when the normal force on the water becomes zero at the highest point.

title: Sign/direction errors
description: Pitfall: Incorrectly assigns signs to forces (e.g., tension direction) or misinterprets the direction of the normal force/pressure.

title: Mass confusion
description: Pitfall: Uses incorrect mass (e.g., cup mass only or water mass only) when calculating the tension for the combined system or the force on the water.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Maintains consistent units throughout the calculation and presents final answers with correct units (N, m/s).
